title: Private deployment: Upgrade cadence playbook, deprecation budget, and cross-team sync cadence
creator: Marisol Vega
description:
Summary:
We need a repeatable, low-friction quarterly playbook for rolling upgrades, deprecation windows, and a small "compatibility budget" that lets Product, Engineering, and Solutions coordinate Private/VPC/on‑prem feature rollouts with minimal customer disruption. The deliverable is a single operational playbook + an automated cadence in the Console (release calendar + notification templates) and a prioritized backlog of non-blocking compatibility fixes for the next two quarters.

Context / Why now:
- Increasing demand from regulated customers for predictable upgrade windows and explicit deprecation policies (legal/IT procurement asks this during contracts).
- Several recent customer upgrade incidents (see incident notes) show friction when we require manual tenant coordination for minor runtime changes.
- Current planning scattered across PM roadmaps and ENG tickets; we lack a unified measure of "compatibility debt" to budget for non-critical but customer-impacting fixes.

Scope (in/out):
- In scope: Quarterly rolling-upgrade playbook (roles/responsibilities), deprecation policy template, compatibility budget definition, Console release calendar UI spec (notifications + tenant opt-in flags), sample comms templates, stakeholder sync cadence, and one pilot with 2 enterprise customers.
- Out of scope: major platform refactors (reserved for Runtime re-arch projects), full automation of tenant upgrade orchestration (follow-up project).

Acceptance criteria:
1) Playbook document in Confluence with step-by-step runbook for a rolling upgrade (pre-checks, safety gates, rollback path, post-mortem template).
2) Compatibility budget defined with a scoring rubric (severity, revert-risk, customer-exposure) and a dashboard card in Console showing budget consumption.
3) Notification templates and legal-friendly deprecation notice wording approved by Legal and Support.
4) Pilot executed with 2 tenants: <Tenant A> and <Tenant B> with post-pilot metrics (successful upgrades, rollback count, customer satisfaction).

Progress updates / Decisions so far:
- 2026-02-18: PM/Eng sync. Decided to prioritize backward-compatible changes first and create a "minor release" lane that uses lower-change risk heuristics. Trade-off: slower feature velocity for tenants choosing strict compatibility.
- 2026-02-25: Draft compatibility scoring rubric created (document link below). Initial rubric focuses on API surface changes, runtime KV-cache invariants, and model-variant compatibility.
- 2026-03-03: Legal and Support reviewed deprecation notice templates; Legal requested inclusion of migration assistance language and SLA-impact disclosure.
- 2026-03-09: Engineering proposed a lightweight Console calendar prototype (mock link). Agreed to ship mock as part of pilot rather than full Console feature in Q2.

Open questions / Trade-offs:
- How big should the compatibility budget be? Proposal: 5% of quarterly eng capacity for compatibility fixes (P1/P2 only). This is a product decision with roadmap trade-offs.
- Opt-in vs opt-out for tenant upgrades: Technical ops prefers opt-in to reduce support load; Sales/Success prefer default opt-in to reduce fragmentation. Proposed compromise: default opt-in with clear SLA and an "Enterprise Lock" flag for tenants who require freeze windows.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Customers may miss deprecation notices. Mitigation: multi-channel notifications (Console banner, email, webhook) and a 90/60/30 day notice cadence.
- Risk: Compatibility fixes accumulate and starve new features. Mitigation: compatibility budget and quarterly review to reprioritize.
- Risk: Legal/regulatory customers require longer freezes. Mitigation: Add "Enterprise Lock" with documented SLAs and a new product offering for extended maintenance windows (follow-up PM ticket).

Implementation plan (high-level milestones):
- Week 1-2: Finalize playbook + rubric; Legal review sign-off on templates.
- Week 3-5: Console calendar mock + pilot instrumentation (dashboard card for compatibility budget).
- Week 6-10: Execute pilot with 2 customers; collect telemetry and CS feedback.
- Week 11-12: Triage pilot results, finalize playbook for Q3 general availability.
